title: Open joy free to change its form

captions.energy: Remaining needed by continually providing leisure
captions.emotions: Feeling an old pleasure’s form end

meaning: Open participation supports leisure when habitual care lets a former format end and hears what both want now.
text: Open participation need not preserve the former way of resting. The Sun in the physical position of Svadhisthana describes a lively exchange of pleasure: showing, sharing and trying together. The Empress in energy leans towards remaining needed by continually providing leisure. Death in emotions allows the ending of an old form of enjoyment to be felt. This may simply mean something familiar no longer pleases. Both need room to keep change separate from judging care. A wish can change while gratitude for earlier pleasure remains.

For example, you enthusiastically prepare the usual supplies for drawing together. Yet both prefer looking at finished pictures and remembering amusing moments. **A former form can end while preserving the value of shared joy.** You can leave new sheets blank and choose today’s conversation. Materials impose no repetition. Care receives a living answer when allowing an ending instead of demanding another completed picture as proof of being needed.

The difficulty is adding paints instead of recognising change. More preparation makes refusal harder and gives an open meeting a hidden obligation. Ending a format may bring sadness without devaluing it. Both can name what has finished and what appeals now. Participation stays real as care supports a new choice rather than holding the old pleasure in place. The earlier experience can remain meaningful without another attempt to reproduce it.
